macro.headline: Bull regime intact but rotation is defensive-tilted; growth pausing.
macro.story:
The tape is mixed but not broken. SPY sits at $749.17, up 3.5% over 21 days and above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, with buying volume still dominant and MACD holding above signal. QQQ, however, has fallen 1.5% over five days, dropped below its 50-day, and flipped MACD negative — the Nasdaq is sideways while the Dow (+5.2% in 21d, RSI 59.7) and Financials lead. VIX at 16.4 is calm (down 15.6% over 21d), but the 10-year yield pushed to 4.61% (RSI 63.9, extended) and the 2-year to 4.26%, flattening the 10Y-2Y spread by 15% over 21 days. Gold (-4.0% in 21d) and Silver (-13.8% in 21d) are broken below both moving averages, while WTI is up 8.3% in 5d and copper is up 5.3%. Breadth is soft under the surface: S&P 500 shows 27% bullish vs 36% bearish names, with 7 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day.

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation is genuinely split, and the substance points to a single causal thread: disinflation and the Fed. The dominant view is that June PPI came in soft (5.5% vs 6.2% expected, core 4.7%) and July rate-hike odds have collapsed to 4% from ~40% just days ago — this is being flagged as the driver of the risk-on tone in refiners, credit-sensitive fintech and select AI names. Countering that, a bearish strain in the conversation is fixated on a single-day IBM collapse as a cautionary tale ('never get comfortable in the AI era'), record foreign outflows from South Korean equities, and Situation Room chatter around a possible Iran offensive and Strait of Hormuz risk. This partially aligns with the data — soft PPI is consistent with the VIX drift lower and Financials leading — but it conflicts with the QQQ breakdown and mega-cap tech pause, which no one in the tracked conversation is cleanly explaining. Refining margins at a record $59/barrel (3-2-1 WTI) are consistent with the Oil & Gas Refining rotation showing up in our own radar.

Under the hood, leadership is Financials (score 9.2, RSI 68.5, HOT), Energy (8.8, HOT) and Utilities (8.2, HOT) — a defensive-plus-cyclical barbell, not a clean risk-on print. Technology and Communication Services are neutral with bearish MACD crosses; Materials and Staples are outright bearish. The validated Early-Runway rotation list is dominated by Healthcare (Diagnostics, Health Info Services, Specialty Pharma), Financials (Credit Services), Energy (Refining) and select Consumer/Comm names — a healthy rotational tape where the hunt is off-index.

Forward watch: whether QQQ reclaims its 50-day (~$720) or rolls to test 200-day support; whether the 10-year yield's extended RSI cools or forces a growth re-rating; and whether any Iran/Hormuz headline reverses the WTI trend and re-prices refining margins. Bull-regime posture stays intact; position sizing should respect the QQQ weakness and the extended yield.

Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.

**[THE SPINE]** Financials leadership on a stable-rates, contained-vol backdrop is the dominant force this week. XLF is +7.7% over 21 days and sitting +6.5% above its 50-day, outpacing every other sector while SPY grinds +3.5% with the VIX crushed to 16.45 and term structure in clean contango. This is not a tech-led tape — Industrials (+6.6%) and Healthcare (+6.1%) are alongside Financials, with XLK a middling +2.8%. The rotation into cyclical/rate-sensitive value on a benign vol regime is the through-line for everything else.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop supports the spine but flashes a caution light on duration. Regime prints CHOPPY with confidence 6/10 and score composition VIX+1 / SPY_vs_50SMA+1 / curve+1 — constructive but not high-conviction. The 10Y is at 4.56% (+2.15% on 21d) and the backtested read is explicit: no ceiling edge — yields continued rising 53% of the time after prior "ceiling" prints, so treat this as trend, not reversion. That's precisely the setup that keeps money in banks/insurers and out of long-duration growth extremes. DXY at 101.02 is grinding higher (+0.98% on 21d) with the DXY_METALS_TAG HOLDS signal in mixed posture — no clean directional call yet, but Gold -3.4%, Silver -13.2%, and the Precious Metals theme is officially FADING. Respect that inverse; it holds in 70% of rolling windows.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into Financials, Industrials, Healthcare, and Utilities — the classic mid-cycle-with-rates-sticky basket. Breadth confirms: 63.6% of sectors above their 50SMA, S&P 500 5d breadth 35.9% bullish vs 21.1% bearish. Rotation flows point INTO Consumer Electronics, Software – Infrastructure, and unmapped names; nothing is being explicitly rotated OUT, which is a benign backdrop, not a defensive one. Semiconductors are the notable exception — XLK trajectory prints ACCELERATING_BULLISH at the sector level, but the Semis industry itself is -11.4% on 21d despite still holding a bullish structure. That divergence matters.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The extended leaders and the in-range setups need to be separated cleanly. Semiconductors are 13 months hot, +258% cumulative — a record run and flagged CEILING; NVDA and AMD show coiled patterns with bullish flow (NVDA coil 87.5%, AMD 78.8%), but the industry-level runway is near zero on historical medians — manage exits, not entries, at the industry level even if single names still coil. The cleaner runway is in early-innings names: Software – Infrastructure just entered a HOT spell at month 1 with only +3% gain — TWLO (coil 70.7%, lean bullish flow) fits. Banks – Regional is choppy but flowing bullish under the surface — USB (coil 86%, bullish) and PNC (coil 84%, lean bullish) map directly onto the Financials spine and haven't extended. AAPL in Consumer Electronics at 96.3% coil with bullish flow is the tightest setup on the board despite the industry being -9.4% on 21d — that's coil-into-strength-of-flow, not a chase.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is XLF holding above its 50SMA combined with the 10Y staying south of the 4.56% resistance that is also its current print. If 10Y breaks 4.60% with conviction and DXY clears 101.80, Financials leadership stays intact but the metals fade accelerates and any remaining duration-sensitive growth trade gets pressured further. If 10Y instead rolls back below 4.42% support with VIX still sub-17, the leadership likely broadens into XLK/QQQ and the semis coil setups (NVDA/AMD) get their trigger. Either way, do not fade the 10Y direction — the data says trend, not ceiling.
